newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet approves pension reform bill.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet approves pension reform bill.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday approved a bill concerning voluntary collective pension schemes, the last of three draft laws that lay the foundations for a crucial reform of the social security system.

"Today the government adopted the third of the package of bills, which are to be a basis for the new pension system. This one is the bill on the workers' pension system," Jerzy Hausner, the cabinet minister steering the reform, told a news briefing.

The bill, which will soon be sent to parliament, provides for creating corporate pension funds to which employers, upon reaching a collective deal with workers, could contribute up to seven percent of the premium now compulsorily paid to the state-owned Social Security Office (ZUS).
Workers would be encouraged to invest in the funds the shares they receive under a special government programme when state firms are privatised, Hausner said.
Under the reform plan, the corporate funds would be one of the sources of pensions beside ZUS, which will continue to operate on the current pay-as-you-go basis.

Another bill on the pension reform, approved earlier in April, envisages the creation of universal pension funds, which will get 20 percent of the sums now paid to ZUS, while the state subsidy for ZUS will increase.
The increase would be financed from privatisation revenues. The ZUS premium now amounts to 45 percent of salaries.

Hausner confirmed that if parliament approved the bills on the pension funds before parliamentary elections, due around September, the reform could be launched in 1999. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
